verifiedClaims.claim: the US-17 / GA-25 (Ocean Highway) corridor — typically near the Broadfield community between Brunswick and Darien, where the 2-lane primary route meets cross-roads like Grants Ferry Road (SR-99)
verifiedClaims.currentValue: US 17 and SR 25 run concurrently through Glynn County; 'Ocean Highway' is the official name (1958 General Assembly resolution). North of Chapel Crossing Road the road drops to two lanes and passes Hofwyl-Broadfield Plantation State Historic Site (5556 US 17 N) before the Altamaha. SR 99 is signed Grants Ferry Road where it meets US 17 in northern Glynn County (GDOT PI 0016985, 'SR 25/US 17 Widening & Reconstruction from Yacht Rd. to SR 99/Grants Ferry Rd.'). That two-lane stretch is being widened to four lanes with a raised median: GDOT reports Phase 1 (Yacht Road to Harry Driggers Blvd) expected open in 2025 and Phase 2 (Harry Driggers Blvd to SR 99) projected 2026, plus a $5.7M roundabout at the US 17 / SR 99 T-intersection; GDOT's 2026-07-31 advisory still lists daily and nightly lane closures with flagging from Yacht Road to SR 99.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia EPD public notice CMV-063-21-02 (GDOT PI 0016985); GDOT 2024 Congressional District 1 update (Purcell report); WTOC GDOT weekly advisory 2026-07-31
verifiedClaims.note: Geography verified. 'Broadfield' as a place name traces to the Broadfield rice plantation on the Altamaha between Darien and Brunswick (New Georgia Encyclopedia; the state historic site is in Glynn County). The '2-lane' description is accurate today but is the subject of an active GDOT widening — the post must say so or it will be wrong within months. EPD notice: https://epd.georgia.gov/document/document/cmv-063-21-02-glynn-county-public-noticepdf/download (Aug 25, 2021; 'widen an approximately 6 mile section of SR 25/US 17 and reconstruct/replace two bridges').

verifiedClaims.claim: evidence (driver logs, ECM data, dashcam footage) can disappear in 30 days unless a preservation letter goes out
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Federal retention floors: records of duty status and supporting documents — 6 months (49 CFR 395.8(k)(1)); driver vehicle inspection reports — 3 months (49 CFR 396.11(a)(4)); maintenance and inspection records — 1 year where the vehicle is housed and 6 months after it leaves the carrier's control (49 CFR 396.3(c)). No federal rule sets a retention period for ECM/EDR data or dashcam video, which carriers may overwrite at any time.
verifiedClaims.note: '30 days' is not a figure from any regulation. Replace with the real floors: HOS logs may be lawfully destroyed after six months, inspection reports after three, and ECM/dashcam data has no federal retention rule at all. The preservation-letter advice stands (it is a litigation practice, not a statute).

verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Code § 51-12-33(g) (Justia); profiles/writer-profile.md jurisdiction table
verifiedClaims.note: § 51-12-33(g): no recovery if the plaintiff is 50 percent or more responsible; (a): damages reduced in proportion to the plaintiff's percentage of fault.

verifiedClaims.note: The FMCSRs apply to motor carriers operating CMVs in interstate commerce (49 CFR 390.3). 'Create direct liability' is a fair lay statement that violations are evidence of negligence; the editor may soften to 'are evidence of negligence against the carrier' if precision is wanted.

verifiedClaims.currentValue: For the second year in a row the Port of Brunswick was the nation's busiest port for automobiles in 2025, handling 779,000 units of autos plus more than 53,000 units of heavy machinery (GPA release, May 4, 2026); GPA describes Brunswick as 'the nation's #1 Ro/Ro gateway'.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Ports Authority press release, 2026-05-04 — 'Port of Brunswick again nation's busiest auto terminal'

No GPA, GDOT or news source places port freight on the Broadfield stretch. Drop the second half of the bullet; keep the port ranking.

verifiedClaims.claim: Glynn County tort lawsuits typically file in Glynn County State Court in Brunswick (Brunswick Judicial Circuit) — though catastrophic claims and diversity cases may go to Glynn County Superior Court or the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Georgia, Brunswick Division.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Glynn County, GA — State Court; O.C.G.A. § 15-7-4; 28 U.S.C. §§ 90(c), 1332; run-4721 facts pack
verifiedClaims.note: State Court of Glynn County 'handles Civil Law Suits' and has civil jurisdiction concurrent with superior court without regard to amount (§ 15-7-4(a)(2)). Superior Court is the Brunswick Judicial Circuit. Brunswick Division of S.D. Ga. covers Glynn (28 U.S.C. § 90(c)). One nit: 'Brunswick Judicial Circuit' describes the Superior Court, not the State Court; the sentence reads as if it labels State Court.

verifiedClaims.claim: Georgia UM/UIM coverage under O.C.G.A. § 33-7-11 is critical when the at-fault trucker is uninsured, underinsured, or absconds — Georgia generally does not permit stacking, so the policy structure matters.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Georgia permits stacking of uninsured/underinsured motorist coverage across multiple policies: 'An insured is permitted to stack multiple policies of uninsured motorist coverage where the tortfeasor is minimally insured' (State Farm v. Hancock, 164 Ga. App. 32 (1982)); 'when more than one source of uninsured motorist coverage is available, claimants may stack the policies' (Dairyland Ins. Co. v. State Farm, Ga. App. 2008). What is not allowed is pyramiding UM limits within a single policy (Crafter v. State Farm, 2001). What actually decides the value of the claim is the written election under § 33-7-11(b)(1)(D)(ii) between 'added-on' coverage (subdivision I, the default) and 'reduced-by' coverage (subdivision II), plus the limits chosen under § 33-7-11(a)(1) — at least $25,000/$50,000/$25,000, or equal to liability limits unless the insured chose less.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Code § 33-7-11 (Justia, 2025 code) and annotated decisions; Dairyland Ins. Co. v. State Farm (Ga. Ct. App. 2008)
verifiedClaims.note: The stacking statement is backwards and is repeated in the body. Dairyland: https://law.justia.com/cases/georgia/court-of-appeals/2008/a07a1919-0.html. Replace with the added-on vs reduced-by election, which is the real 'policy structure' point. Also: an absconding (hit-and-run) driver is 'uninsured' under § 33-7-11(b)(2) only with physical contact or a corroborating eyewitness.

verifiedClaims.claim: A wrongful-death claim under O.C.G.A. § 51-4-1 et seq. belongs to the spouse, children, or parents — separate from the estate's survival claim — and the 2-year clock applies the same way.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Code §§ 51-4-1, 51-4-2(a), 19-7-1(c)(2) (Justia); § 9-3-33 annotations (run-4721)
verifiedClaims.note: § 51-4-2(a): surviving spouse, or if none, the children, recover the full value of the life; § 19-7-1(c)(2): parents recover when no spouse or child survives. Georgia courts apply the § 9-3-33 two-year period to wrongful-death actions (verified in run-4721).

verifiedClaims.claim: US-17 and GA-25 share the same alignment through Glynn County under the name "Ocean Highway." It is a 2-lane primary route that parallels I-95 a few miles to the west
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Concurrency and the Ocean Highway name are correct. The road is four lanes through and just north of Brunswick and two lanes from north of Chapel Crossing Road to the Altamaha; GDOT is widening the Yacht Road–SR 99 segment to four lanes (see first claim). I-95 runs to the west of US 17 through Glynn County (SR 99/Grants Ferry Road connects the two at exit 42).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: GDOT 2024 CD1 update; EPD notice PI 0016985; U.S. Route 17 in Georgia route description (GDOT county maps)
verifiedClaims.note: Add the widening status so the '2-lane' description does not go stale. 'Primary route' is not a GDOT classification term; say 'two-lane U.S. highway'.

verifiedClaims.claim: Speed limits along US-17 typically run 55 mph between developed pockets and drop to 35–45 mph through residential stretches like Broadfield.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Georgia's statutory maximum is 55 mph 'in other locations' (O.C.G.A. § 40-6-181(b)(5)) and 30 mph in any urban or residential district unless otherwise posted ((b)(1)); the widened four-lane section is designed for 55 mph. No GDOT source publishes the posted limits at Broadfield.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Code § 40-6-181 (Justia)

verifiedClaims.claim: There is no continuous center turn lane through most of the corridor. Driveway curb-cuts are frequent. Left-turn-across-path crashes are common.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: The GDOT widening replaces the undivided two-lane section with four lanes, a raised median and auxiliary turn lanes at median openings, and adds a roundabout at the US 17 / SR 99 T-intersection. Nationally, in 7.9% of two-vehicle fatal large-truck crashes the other vehicle was turning left (NHTSA, 2023 data).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: GDOT 2024 CD1 update; NHTSA Traffic Safety Facts: Large Trucks, 2023 data (DOT HS 813 717), Table 5 discussion
verifiedClaims.note: The absence of a median/turn lanes on the two-lane section is implicit in GDOT's project scope, but 'left-turn-across-path crashes are common' on this corridor has no GDOT, GOHS or FARS source. Keep the geometry as a present-tense description of the unwidened section, drop 'are common', and note the median and turn lanes the project adds.

verifiedClaims.claim: According to the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA), large trucks were involved in 5,837 fatal crashes nationwide in 2022 — and in 73% of those fatal two-vehicle crashes, the truck struck the other vehicle.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: NHTSA (FARS): 5,375 large trucks were involved in fatal crashes in 2023, down from 5,873 in 2022. 5,472 people were killed in large-truck crashes in 2023 (an 8% decrease from 5,969 in 2022), and 70% of them (3,837) were occupants of other vehicles. 80% of large trucks in fatal crashes were in multi-vehicle crashes. In two-vehicle fatal crashes the truck and the other vehicle hit front-to-front 32.1% of the time; trucks were struck from the rear 3 times as often as the other vehicle (21.2% vs 6.3%).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: NHTSA, Traffic Safety Facts: Large Trucks — 2023 Data (DOT HS 813 717)
verifiedClaims.note: Three problems: the 2022 figure is transposed (5,873, not 5,837); it is a year stale; and '73% ... the truck struck the other vehicle' is not a statistic NHTSA or FMCSA publishes — the nearest real figure is that 70% of the dead were occupants of the other vehicle. FMCSA's own Large Truck and Bus Crash Facts page returned 403 to automated fetch, so attribute to NHTSA, whose fact sheet is the FARS source both agencies use.

verifiedClaims.claim: According to the Georgia Department of Transportation (GDOT), US-17 is classified as part of Georgia's National Highway System primary route network — a designation that recognizes its role as a freight corridor parallel to I-95 along the entire Georgia coast.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: FHWA National Highway System maps — Georgia / Brunswick, GA

US 17 in Georgia is on the NHS only from US 82/SR 303/SR 520 west of Brunswick to SR 25 Spur in Brunswick, and from southwest of Richmond Hill to the South Carolina line (FHWA NHS maps, as summarized in the U.S. Route 17 in Georgia route description). The Broadfield stretch is not NHS, 'primary route network' is not an NHS or GDOT term, and GDOT makes no 'freight corridor parallel to I-95 along the entire coast' designation. Delete the paragraph.

verifiedClaims.claim: preserve the truck's ECM (engine control module) data, hours-of-service logs, dashcam footage, dispatch records, and maintenance files. Under federal regulations these records can be lawfully overwritten on short cycles.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Hours-of-service records and supporting documents: 6 months (49 CFR 395.8(k)); driver vehicle inspection reports: 3 months (49 CFR 396.11); maintenance/inspection records: 1 year plus 6 months after the vehicle leaves the carrier (49 CFR 396.3(c)). ECM/EDR data and dashcam video carry no federal retention requirement.
verifiedClaims.note: 'Short cycles' is acceptable but vague; the concrete floors are more persuasive and are the point of the letter. Note the ELD retention rule is at 395.8(k), with ELD technical retention in 395.22; eCFR redirected automated fetches, so LII is the verified mirror.

verifiedClaims.claim: If the crash involves a city vehicle (Brunswick, Darien) you must serve ante-litem notice within 6 months under O.C.G.A. § 36-33-5. If the crash involves a state vehicle or the State of Georgia, you must serve ante-litem notice within 12 months under O.C.G.A. § 50-21-26.

verifiedClaims.note: § 36-33-5: claim presented in writing 'within six months of the happening of the event'; § 50-21-26(a)(1): notice in writing within 12 months of when the loss was discovered or should have been discovered. Gap: a Glynn County (county government) vehicle is governed by O.C.G.A. § 36-11-1 — claims against counties must be presented within 12 months — and the post never mentions counties. The year-less Justia URL for § 36-33-5 currently redirects to the 2022 edition (https://law.justia.com/codes/georgia/2022/title-36/chapter-33/section-36-33-5/); it resolves.

verifiedClaims.currentValue: § 51-1-40(b): a seller or server may be liable only if it 'knowingly sells, furnishes, or serves alcoholic beverages to a person who is in a state of noticeable intoxication, knowing that such person will soon be driving a motor vehicle' (or willfully serves a minor knowing the same), and the service is the proximate cause of the injury.

verifiedClaims.claim: Georgia generally does not permit stacking across multiple policies, which makes the original offer-of-reduction form and the structure of your auto policy decisive.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Georgia permits stacking of UM/UIM coverage across multiple policies (Hancock, 1982; Dairyland, 2008), though not pyramiding within one policy. The decisive document is the written election under § 33-7-11(b)(1)(D)(ii): 'added-on' coverage (the default) pays on top of the trucker's liability limits; 'reduced-by' coverage, which the insured may select in writing, pays only the difference between those limits and the UM limits.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Code § 33-7-11(b)(1)(D)(ii) and annotations (Justia); Dairyland Ins. Co. v. State Farm (Ga. Ct. App. 2008)
verifiedClaims.note: Repeats the reversed stacking claim from the Key Takeaways. 'Offer-of-reduction form' is not a Georgia term; the statute speaks of rejecting added-on coverage and selecting reduced-by coverage in writing.

verifiedClaims.claim: on the coastal corridor, where out-of-state and minimum-limits drivers are common, this is often the difference between a real recovery and a paper victory.
verifiedClaims.note: No primary source publishes out-of-state or minimum-limits driver shares for the Georgia coast (run-4721 reached the same conclusion for uninsured rates; the only figure is statewide and from the Insurance Research Council, outside the source set). Drop the 'are common' clause; the UM advice stands on § 33-7-11 and the $25,000 minimum.

verifiedClaims.claim: Glynn County State Court, which handles non-felony civil tort matters and is the typical venue for personal-injury cases. Glynn County Superior Court (part of the Brunswick Judicial Circuit) handles felony-related tort matters and larger equity issues.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: State courts have jurisdiction, concurrent with the superior courts, over 'the trial of civil actions without regard to the amount in controversy, except those actions in which exclusive jurisdiction is vested in the superior courts' and criminal cases below the grade of felony (O.C.G.A. § 15-7-4(a)). The Superior Court (Brunswick Judicial Circuit) is the court of general jurisdiction with exclusive jurisdiction over felonies, divorce, equity and title to land; a personal-injury suit may be filed in either court.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Code § 15-7-4 (Justia); Judicial Council of Georgia — Navigating the Courts; Glynn County — State Court
verifiedClaims.note: 'Non-felony civil tort matters' and 'felony-related tort matters' are not categories Georgia law uses — felonies are criminal, and civil damages claims have no felony/non-felony split. State Court's civil jurisdiction has no dollar cap. Rewrite both sentences to the concurrent-jurisdiction rule. georgiacourts.gov: https://georgiacourts.gov/a2j/self-help-resources/navigating-the-courts/.

verifiedClaims.claim: Glynn County Magistrate Court handles small claims under $15,000.

verifiedClaims.claim: Cases with diversity of citizenship — for example, a Florida-based motor carrier sued by a Georgia plaintiff for more than $75,000 — often end up in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Georgia, Brunswick Division.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: 28 U.S.C. § 1332(a); 28 U.S.C. § 90(c) (Cornell LII); S.D. Ga. Brunswick office; run-4721 facts pack
verifiedClaims.note: Amount in controversy exceeding $75,000 and complete diversity; Brunswick Division comprises Appling, Camden, Glynn, Jeff Davis, Long, McIntosh and Wayne. Courthouse at 801 Gloucester Street, Brunswick.

verifiedClaims.claim: Eric is admitted to practice in Georgia and has spent more than two decades representing injured people and grieving families across the Georgia coast
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Admitted in Georgia (correct). J.D. University of Georgia School of Law, 2012 — about 14 years in practice.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: UGA School of Law — Spotlight: Eric Roden (J.D.'12); client.json barStates GA
verifiedClaims.note: Second instance of the 'two decades' claim. Keep 'admitted to practice in Georgia'; remove the tenure figure or change to 'more than a decade'.

verifiedClaims.claim: Roden Law operates a Darien office at 1108 North Way, Darien, Georgia 31305, approximately 12–15 miles north of the Broadfield cluster along US-17.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Office address matches client.json (1108 North Way, Darien, GA 31305). Hofwyl-Broadfield Plantation (31.305 N, 81.454 W) is about 4.7 miles straight-line south of downtown Darien (31.370 N, 81.434 W); the drive up US 17 across the Altamaha delta is on the order of 6–7 miles, not 12–15. (Brunswick is about 11 miles straight-line to the south.)
verifiedClaims.sourceName: client.json (locations: Darien); Hofwyl-Broadfield Plantation coordinates (Georgia DNR state historic site, 5556 US 17 N)
verifiedClaims.note: The mileage is wrong by roughly double — the post appears to have used the Brunswick-to-Darien distance. No agency publishes the road distance, so say 'a few miles north of Broadfield on US-17' or 'under 10 miles' rather than a precise figure.

verifiedClaims.claim: Hit by a big rig on US-17 / GA-25 through Broadfield in Glynn County? A Georgia truck accident lawyer's guide to deadlines, fault, and recovery.
verifiedClaims.note: No factual claim beyond the corridor designation, which is verified.

verifiedClaims.claim: Under O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33, you have 2 years from the date of injury to file a personal-injury lawsuit in Georgia. If a government vehicle was involved, ante-litem notice is required much sooner — 6 months for a city under O.C.G.A. § 36-33-5, 12 months for the state under O.C.G.A. § 50-21-26.
verifiedClaims.note: All three periods verified. Optional but recommended: add '12 months for a county under O.C.G.A. § 36-11-1' since a Glynn County vehicle is the likeliest government defendant on this corridor. FAQ answers publish as FAQPage structured data.

verifiedClaims.claim: Georgia uses modified comparative negligence at O.C.G.A. § 51-12-33, with a 50% bar. If you are found 49% at fault, you recover 51% of your damages. If you are 50% or more at fault, you recover nothing.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Code § 51-12-33(a), (g) (Justia)
verifiedClaims.note: Rule and arithmetic correct.

verifiedClaims.claim: Most Glynn County personal-injury suits are filed in Glynn County State Court in Brunswick, part of the Brunswick Judicial Circuit. Larger or felony-adjacent cases go to Glynn County Superior Court. Federal cases with diversity jurisdiction file in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Georgia, Brunswick Division.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: State Court of Glynn County hears civil suits without regard to amount, concurrently with the Superior Court (O.C.G.A. § 15-7-4(a)(2)); the Superior Court of Glynn County (Brunswick Judicial Circuit) is the court of general jurisdiction. Either can hear a truck-crash suit; there is no 'larger' or 'felony-adjacent' threshold. Federal venue with diversity and more than $75,000 at stake is the Brunswick Division of the Southern District of Georgia.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Code § 15-7-4 (Justia); Glynn County — State Court; 28 U.S.C. §§ 90(c), 1332
verifiedClaims.note: Two errors: the Brunswick Judicial Circuit is the Superior Court's circuit, not State Court's; and 'larger or felony-adjacent cases go to Superior Court' misstates concurrent civil jurisdiction. Published twice (FAQPage schema).

verifiedClaims.claim: Interstate trucking triggers the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations (49 C.F.R.) on top of Georgia tort law, and the case may be removable to federal court. Out-of-state carriers also have to answer to USDOT compliance records, hours-of-service logs, and electronic ECM data that a Georgia attorney can subpoena early.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: 49 CFR Parts 390–396 (Cornell LII); 28 U.S.C. §§ 1332, 1441
verifiedClaims.note: Accurate. 'Subpoena' is loose (most of this comes through discovery requests and the preservation letter), but not wrong.

verifiedClaims.claim: A DUI conviction under O.C.G.A. § 40-6-391 is persuasive evidence in your civil case and frequently supports a punitive-damages claim. If a Glynn County bar or restaurant over-served the driver before the crash, Georgia's dram-shop statute at O.C.G.A. § 51-1-40 may open a separate claim against the establishment.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Punitive damages: under O.C.G.A. § 51-12-5.1(f), when the defendant acted while under the influence of alcohol or drugs to the degree that judgment was substantially impaired, 'there shall be no limitation regarding the amount which may be awarded as punitive damages against an active tort-feasor' (the $250,000 cap in subsection (g) does not apply). Dram shop: liability requires knowingly serving a noticeably intoxicated person while knowing they will soon drive (§ 51-1-40(b)).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Code § 51-12-5.1(f) (Justia, canonical path section-51-12-5-1); § 51-1-40(b); § 40-6-391
verifiedClaims.note: Nothing false, but two upgrades: (1) the uncapped-punitives rule for impaired drivers is the strongest point available and is missing; (2) 'over-served' should track the statute's 'noticeably intoxicated ... knowing that such person will soon be driving'. FAQ text feeds FAQPage schema.

verifiedClaims.claim: Nothing upfront. Roden Law handles truck-accident cases on contingency — we advance the costs of investigation, accident reconstruction, and expert witnesses, and you owe no legal fees unless we recover money for you. The initial consultation is free, and you can reach us at 1-844-RESULTS.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Firm's own fee representation; theme firm data (vanity_phone 844-RESULTS; run-4721)
verifiedClaims.note: Firm policy, not an external fact; phone matches the theme's canonical vanity number.

recommendedEdits: Intro paragraph: delete 'bound for the Port of Brunswick, cutting around an interstate weigh station, or' — the port terminal is on US 17 south of Brunswick and there is no I-95 inspection station in Glynn County; keep 'threading the Broadfield curves with summer tourists'.

Intro and 'Why US-17' section: after describing the two-lane stretch, add one sentence: 'GDOT is widening US-17 from Yacht Road to SR 99 (Grants Ferry Road) to four lanes with a raised median — Phase 1 was expected to open in 2025 and Phase 2 in 2026 — and is building a roundabout at the US-17 / SR 99 intersection; as of July 2026 lane closures with flagging were still in place.' Cite GDOT.

Key Takeaways, evidence bullet: replace 'can disappear in 30 days' with 'can be lawfully destroyed after as little as three months (inspection reports, 49 CFR 396.11) or six months (hours-of-service records, 49 CFR 395.8(k)), and ECM and dashcam data have no federal retention rule at all'.

Key Takeaways, port bullet: replace with 'The Port of Brunswick was the nation's busiest port for automobiles in 2025 for the second straight year, handling 779,000 vehicles (Georgia Ports Authority)' and delete 'freight bound for or from the port routinely funnels onto US-17 / GA-25 and creates a heavy-truck mix on a 2-lane primary road'.

Key Takeaways, UM/UIM bullet: replace 'Georgia generally does not permit stacking, so the policy structure matters' with 'Georgia lets you stack UM coverage across multiple policies, and whether you elected "added-on" or "reduced-by" coverage under § 33-7-11 decides how much of it survives the trucker's liability limits'.
Key Takeaways, venue bullet: move '(Brunswick Judicial Circuit)' so it modifies Glynn County Superior Court, not State Court.

'Why US-17' section, paragraph 1: delete 'And Port of Brunswick freight diverts onto US-17 to bypass interstate weigh stations or to reach local Glynn County destinations.' and change 'That mix is the problem.' to refer to commuters, tourists and local delivery trucks.

'Why US-17' section, paragraph 2: replace 'Speed limits along US-17 typically run 55 mph between developed pockets and drop to 35–45 mph through residential stretches like Broadfield' with 'Georgia's statutory limit on a two-lane highway like this is 55 mph (O.C.G.A. § 40-6-181), lower only where posted'; delete 'Left-turn-across-path crashes are common.' and add that the widening adds a median and turn lanes.

FMCSA paragraph: replace with 'According to NHTSA, 5,375 large trucks were involved in fatal crashes nationwide in 2023 (down from 5,873 in 2022), 5,472 people died in those crashes, and 70% of the dead were occupants of the other vehicle, not the truck.' Cite NHTSA Traffic Safety Facts: Large Trucks, 2023 data (DOT HS 813 717). Remove the '73% ... the truck struck the other vehicle' sentence entirely.

GDOT / National Highway System paragraph: delete it. US-17 through Broadfield is not on the NHS (only the Brunswick segment west of SR 25 Spur and the Richmond Hill-to-SC segment are), and 'primary route network' is not a GDOT designation.

GOHS paragraph: replace with 'According to the Governor's Office of Highway Safety, Georgia recorded 1,615 traffic fatalities in 2023, down 10% from 1,796 in 2022; one-third of the state's fatal crashes happen in rural areas that hold only 21% of its population, 45% involve a vehicle leaving its lane or the road, and 12% involve a large truck.' Drop 'fits that profile exactly' or tie it to those rural/roadway-departure figures.
Comparison table, Speed limit row: change '35–55 mph, varies by stretch' to '55 mph maximum; lower where posted'.
Comparison table, Median row: change 'None through most of the corridor' to 'None on the two-lane section; a raised median is being added in the current widening'.
Comparison table, Tourist exposure row: delete the row (no per-mile risk statistic exists for either corridor).
Comparison table, Weigh-station row: change to 'I-95: yes, in McIntosh County at MM 55/56 north of Darien (none in Glynn County) | US-17: none' and delete 'a known bypass route'.

'First 72 Hours', step 1: replace 'severe cases are typically transferred to Memorial Health University Medical Center in Savannah for Level I trauma care' with 'Memorial Health University Medical Center in Savannah is the region's only Level I trauma center; Southeast Georgia Health System's Brunswick Campus is the county hospital.' Do not describe SGHS as a trauma center or assert a transfer pathway.

'First 72 Hours', step 3: change 'Georgia State Patrol or Glynn County Sheriff's Office' to 'Georgia State Patrol (Post 23, Brunswick) or the Glynn County Police Department, whose Records Section releases crash reports'.

'First 72 Hours', step 5: replace 'Under federal regulations these records can be lawfully overwritten on short cycles' with 'Federal rules require carriers to keep hours-of-service records for only six months (49 CFR 395.8(k)) and inspection reports for three (49 CFR 396.11); ECM and dashcam data have no retention rule.'
Statute-of-limitations paragraph: add 'If the crash involves a Glynn County vehicle, claims against the county must be presented within 12 months under O.C.G.A. § 36-11-1.'
Eric Roden paragraph and About the Author: delete 'more than two decades' in both places (J.D. 2012); change 'The first 30 days are not paperwork' to 'The first weeks are not paperwork'.

DUI section: delete 'Late-night drunk-driver crashes on US-17 through Glynn County are a recurring pattern, especially during summer beach season.'; change 'was over-served at a Glynn County bar or restaurant' to 'was knowingly served while noticeably intoxicated by a Glynn County bar or restaurant that knew he would soon be driving'.

UM paragraph: replace 'Georgia generally does not permit stacking across multiple policies, which makes the original offer-of-reduction form and the structure of your auto policy decisive' with 'Georgia lets you stack UM coverage from more than one policy, and the written election you made between "added-on" and "reduced-by" coverage under O.C.G.A. § 33-7-11 decides whether your UM limits sit on top of the trucker's policy or are reduced by it'; delete 'where out-of-state and minimum-limits drivers are common,'.

Venue section: rewrite the first two sentences: 'Most Glynn County truck-crash suits are filed in Glynn County State Court in Brunswick, which hears civil actions without regard to the amount in controversy (O.C.G.A. § 15-7-4). Glynn County Superior Court, the Brunswick Judicial Circuit's court of general jurisdiction, can hear the same suits and has exclusive jurisdiction over felonies, divorce, equity and title to land.' Change 'small claims under $15,000' to 'civil claims of $15,000 or less'.

About the Author: replace 'approximately 12–15 miles north of the Broadfield cluster along US-17' with 'a few miles north of Broadfield on US-17' (the historic site is under five miles from Darien as the crow flies).
FAQ 1 (index 0): optionally append '— and 12 months for a county under O.C.G.A. § 36-11-1'.

FAQ 3 (index 2): replace with 'Most Glynn County personal-injury suits are filed in Glynn County State Court in Brunswick, which hears civil cases of any amount; Glynn County Superior Court (Brunswick Judicial Circuit) can hear the same cases. Suits against an out-of-state carrier for more than $75,000 may be filed in or removed to the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Georgia, Brunswick Division.'

FAQ 5 (index 4): after 'frequently supports a punitive-damages claim' add '— and Georgia's $250,000 cap on punitive damages does not apply when the driver was impaired (O.C.G.A. § 51-12-5.1(f))'; change 'over-served the driver' to 'knowingly served the driver while he was noticeably intoxicated and about to drive'.
